title: Understanding Developer Pain Points in Federated Learning: Insights from Stack Overflow and GitHub
task: Identifying federated-learning developer challenges from Q&A posts and issue trackers
problem: Federated-learning frameworks are hard to set up and operate, but developer challenges were not systematically characterised across platforms.
architecture: BERTopic with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, UMAP and a bigram CountVectorizer; topics labelled by three authors from keywords and 10-30 sampled artifacts; difficulty measured by unresolved rate and median resolution time; question-intent (How/Why/What) analysis.

datasets.name: Stack Overflow
datasets.details: 495 FL-related posts (from 164 seed posts and co-occurring tags)

datasets.name: GitHub
datasets.details: 9,116 issues and pull requests from 92 FL repositories

key_results: 9 Stack Overflow topics and 13 GitHub topics; largest SO topic 'TFF Implementation & Client' has 167 posts.
'TFF Installation & Environment Compatibility' has 82.22% of posts without an accepted answer; 'PySyft Setup & API Breakages' has the longest median time (99.19 h).
strengths: Cross-platform comparison with explicit difficulty indicators.

limitations.text: Only public discussions and a subset of widely discussed frameworks; percentages for small topics are unstable.
Topic quality is not evaluated with coherence/diversity or against another topic model.
